s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive symmetric small joint pain with morning stiffness and fatigue
salient_findings: Symmetric pain in small joints of hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
Early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
Severe fatigue throughout the day
Recent mild COVID-19 infection
Elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
Synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI
key_facts: 4 months of progressively worsening symptoms
Symmetric joint pain
Early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
Severe fatigue throughout the day
Recent mild COVID-19 infection confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR
No fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, rash, or appetite changes since recovering
No recent genitourinary or gastrointestinal infections
No history of psoriasis or uveitis
Family history of rheumatoid arthritis
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 13 mm/hour
C-reactive protein of 4.3 mg/L
Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640
Rheumatoid factor of 62.29 IU/mL
Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody of 237.39 units
Hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
Radiographs of hands, knees, ankles, and feet were unremarkable
Hand ultrasound showed no joint erosion
MRI of hands demonstrated synovitis and tenosynovitis

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: High levels of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, symmetric joint pain, and morning stiffness

shortlist.label: Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, consistent with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated antinuclear antibody titer and presence of fatigue, although other criteria are not fully met

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of symptoms with rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, and high antinuclear antibody titer

shortlist.label: COVID-19 associated arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent history of COVID-19 infection, which can trigger various forms of arthritis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of symmetric joint pain, early morning stiffness, and severe fatigue, combined with laboratory results showing a positive rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, are consistent with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. The family history of rheumatoid arthritis also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis, the presence of a positive rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody specifically supports a diagnosis of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory results do not show double-stranded DNA antibodies, which are often present in systemic lupus erythematosus, and there are no other symptoms suggestive of this diagnosis

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not meet the criteria for mixed connective tissue disease, which typically includes a combination of features from multiple autoimmune diseases

rejected.label: COVID-19 associated arthritis
rejected.why: While the patient had a recent COVID-19 infection, the duration and nature of her symptoms are more consistent with a chronic autoimmune condition like seropositive rheumatoid arthritis
